_doc.purpose: Single source of truth for the 'second brain' decision-support project. Edited collaboratively across sessions. Diffable, versionable, and consumable by both humans and LLMs as context for future design and build conversations.
_doc.edit_protocol: When changing a field, bump meta.version, add a changelog entry with date + what changed + why, and (for revisions of load-bearing facts) move the old value into _superseded with a note. Never silently overwrite.

assumptions.claim: Personal DB + RAG materially reduces hallucinations and produces meaningfully better answers than strong single-model with good context
assumptions.verdict: Premature. Hand-curated context file gets 70-80% of the benefit at 5% of complexity. RAG earns its keep at hundreds of documents, which is years away for personal use.

assumptions.claim: Multi-model critique (council of 3) produces better answers than single strong model
assumptions.verdict: Mostly theater for this use case. Real value the user observes from manual cross-posting comes from the human-in-the-loop iterating, not from models judging each other. Defer indefinitely.

assumptions.claim: Can build competitive deep research from scratch
assumptions.verdict: Reframe: not building OpenAI/Gemini/Claude/Perplexity Deep Research clones. Building Karpathy-style overnight agent runs that decompose a question against personal context.

assumptions.claim: More memory is monotonically better (know everything)
assumptions.verdict: False at scale. Stale facts and signal-to-noise problems emerge. Useful memory = stable identity + current goals + recent decisions and outcomes. Not 'everything'.

assumptions.claim: I will use this daily as my default thinking surface
assumptions.verdict: Uncertain. 8 years of not building for self is the base rate against. Bench window and narrow scope improve odds.
Friends are kind, share biases, and onboarding cost (telling it 'everything') is huge. Useful as forcing function only. Removed from v1.

assumptions.claim: $50/mo is enough to run the system
assumptions.verdict: Yes, with single-model + cost-aware routing (cheap model for simple sub-queries, frontier for decomposition/synthesis). 1 overnight run/week ~ $5-20/mo.

assumptions.claim: Brain first, tool suite later is the right order
assumptions.verdict: Correct ordering. Just needs the brain itself defined narrowly.

concept_v1.name: Narrow personal-context overnight research agent
concept_v1.audience: Technical professionals (starting with the user) running multiple parallel high-stakes life deliberations who already triangulate manually across LLMs, research, and human experts
concept_v1.exact_problem: One big life question decomposes into a web of sub-questions across finance, culture, family, timing, logistics, legal - each needing real personal context to answer usefully. Currently done in head, manually chased across tools, stitched together by hand. Hours of work and synthesis lives only in the user's head.
concept_v1.job_to_be_done: When I have a multi-domain life decision that matters, help me decompose it into the right sub-questions, research each thread against my actual situation, and give me back one synthesized 2-page answer I can act on - with the full audit trail preserved if I want to dig.
when_useful: Marriage / house / PR / career-pivot class questions
when_not_useful: Quick facts, code help, casual chat, creative writing - these go to Claude.ai directly

why_existing_tools_insufficient.gap: Hold static context but don't decompose or run multi-step research autonomously

why_existing_tools_insufficient.tool: OpenAI / Gemini / Claude / Perplexity Deep Research
why_existing_tools_insufficient.gap: Decompose and research well but stateless about the user - don't know income, family, cultural context, timeline
Built for coding, not personal decision support
Know the user but don't reason deeply or run research agents

concept_v1.differentiator: Combines personal context (knows the user) with autonomous multi-step decomposition + research (Karpathy-style overnight agent loop). Nothing on the market combines both for consumers.

must_haves.name: Hand-curated personal context file
must_haves.detail: Markdown, 2-3 pages, user-maintained. No RAG, no extraction, no graph DB.
must_haves.rationale: Lowest-cost way to get 70-80% of personalization benefit; teaches what categories actually matter before committing to infrastructure

must_haves.name: Question decomposition step
must_haves.detail: Model takes parent question + context file, emits a tree of sub-questions with a reasoning plan
must_haves.rationale: The core differentiator; mimics user's natural deliberation process

must_haves.name: Overnight research loop
must_haves.detail: Agent loop works through sub-questions one at a time, uses web search where needed, preserves intermediate findings
must_haves.rationale: Karpathy-style; the actual mechanism that justifies the wait

must_haves.name: Synthesis pass
must_haves.detail: One model reads all intermediate findings + context file, produces 2-page summary with recommendation

must_haves.name: Audit trail preserved
must_haves.detail: Intermediate sub-answers live in a file the user can open later
must_haves.rationale: Reviewing the system's reasoning is how the user learns from it; satisfies the resume/learning quit condition

must_haves.name: Text interface only
must_haves.detail: Terminal, CLI, or dead-simple local web UI. No mobile, no voice, no Play Store.
must_haves.rationale: Anything else is scope creep on a first project

must_haves.name: Cost-aware model routing
must_haves.detail: Cheap model (Haiku/mini class) for simple sub-queries; frontier model for decomposition and synthesis
must_haves.rationale: Keeps under $50/mo ceiling; also a resume-grade skill
